completeness.reason: All three mandated record fields, the non-volatile storage and the diagnostic readout are covered, but the obligation that the record 'remains readable over the diagnostic interface after a power cycle' is covered only shallowly - there is no integrity or power-loss-during-write protection for the record.
completeness.suggestion: Add the record integrity mechanism (checksum or CRC per record, and how a torn write is detected and discarded on readout) so post-power-cycle readability is designed rather than assumed.

consistency.reason: No sibling shares REQ_FAULT_RECORD, and the element does not contradict any related element: the supervisor emits the record it stores, and its reset-forwarding ordering complements the supervisor's latch exit rather than competing with it.

design_clarity.reason: Names concrete choices (64-entry ring in NVM, fixed 16-byte layout, four named fields, reset forwarded only after the active fault's record is written) but leaves a material storage detail unspecified: what happens when the ring wraps - overwrite the oldest record or stop accepting new ones.
design_clarity.suggestion: State the wrap policy for the 64-entry ring explicitly (overwrite-oldest vs freeze-on-full) since a safety fault log's evidence value depends on it.

implementability.reason: Realisable and bounded, but an implementer must decide the wrap policy, the integrity scheme, and the exact handshake by which 'the record of the active fault has been written' is confirmed before the reset is forwarded.
implementability.suggestion: Specify the write-then-forward handshake (e.g. forward the reset only after the NVM write has been read back and verified) and note that this element consumes the diagnostic service reset that REQ_FAULT_LATCH mandates - consider linking it to REQ_FAULT_LATCH as well, since it owns part of that obligation's path.

parent_fit.reason: Substantively addresses REQ_FAULT_RECORD: it owns the non-volatile record store, its layout carries the cell/sensor identifier, the violated-limit identifier and the measured value, and it serves the records over the diagnostic interface.

summary: Record content and the reset handshake are well chosen, but for a non-volatile safety log the storage design is thin: no wrap policy on the 64-entry ring and no integrity mechanism, even though the parent requires the record to still be readable after a power cycle - and the sibling ARCH_SOC_STORE shows the project knows how to do this (two slots plus checksum).
